q007.answer_text: A healthcare organisation deploying an AI-enabled medical device that qualifies as a high-risk AI system under the AI Act must, as a provider, submit specific information for registration in the EU database before placing the system on the market or putting it into service. This includes: the provider's name, address, and contact details; details of any authorised representative; the AI system's trade name and unambiguous reference; a description of the intended purpose of the AI system and its components and functions; a basic description of the data inputs and operating logic; the system's market status; certificate details from the notified body (if applicable), including a scanned copy; Member States where the system is available; a copy of the EU declaration of conformity; electronic instructions for use; and an optional URL for additional information. The organisation must also ensure conformity with relevant Union harmonisation legislation (such as the Medical Devices Regulation) and may need to follow specific conformity assessment procedures, potentially involving notified bodies, depending on the device classification. Additionally, if the organisation considers the AI system not high-risk despite its inclusion in Annex III, it must document this assessment prior to market placement and be subject to registration under Article 49(2).

claims.text: Providers of high-risk AI systems must submit the name, address, and contact details of the provider for registration.
Providers must submit the name, address, and contact details of any authorised representative, where applicable.
Providers must submit the AI system trade name and any additional unambiguous reference allowing identification and traceability.
Providers must submit a description of the intended purpose of the AI system and of the components and functions supported through this AI system.
Providers must submit a basic and concise description of the information used by the system (data, inputs) and its operating logic.
Providers must submit the status of the AI system (on the market, in service, no longer placed on the market/in service, or recalled).
Providers must submit the type, number, and expiry date of the certificate issued by the notified body and the name or identification number of that notified body, where applicable.
Providers must submit a scanned copy of the certificate referred to in the notified body certificate point, where applicable.
Providers must submit any Member States in which the AI system has been placed on the market, put into service, or made available in the Union.
Providers must submit a copy of the EU declaration of conformity referred to in Article 47.
Providers must submit electronic instructions for use, except for high-risk AI systems in law enforcement, migration, asylum, and border control management.
Providers may optionally submit a URL for additional information.

A provider who considers that an AI system referred to in Annex III is not high-risk shall document its assessment before that system is placed on the market or put into service and shall be subject to the registration obligation set out in Article 49(2).
Council Directive 93/42/EEC concerns medical devices.

final_report.overview: The AI Act imposes distinct pre-market and post-market obligations on non-EU manufacturers/providers, EU importers, EU distributors, and healthcare organisations deploying AI-enabled medical devices. Non-EU providers must appoint an EU authorised representative and register the system pre-market; post-market obligations for non-EU providers are not detailed in the evidence. EU importers have pre-market verification and documentation duties, and post-market duties including risk reporting, conformity checks, and cooperation with authorities. EU distributor obligations (both pre- and post-market) lack sufficient evidence. Healthcare organisations, as providers, must register and ensure conformity pre-market; post-market obligations for deployers are not specified in the evidence.

sections.title: Non-EU Manufacturer/Provider - Pre-market Obligations
sections.answer_text: Prior to placing a high-risk AI-enabled medical device on the Union market, a non-EU provider must, by written mandate, appoint an authorised representative established in the Union. The provider must ensure the authorised representative can verify the EU declaration of conformity and technical documentation, keep documentation available for 10 years, provide information to competent authorities, cooperate on risk mitigation, and ensure registration information is correct. The provider must also register the high-risk AI system in the EU database, submitting information including name and contact details, authorised representative details, AI system trade name, description of intended purpose and components, data and operating logic, system status, certificate details from the notified body, scanned certificate copy, Member States where placed on market, EU declaration of conformity, electronic instructions for use, and an optional URL for additional information, keeping this information up to date.

sections.title: Non-EU Manufacturer/Provider - Post-market Obligations
sections.answer_text: The provided evidence does not contain specific information about the post-market obligations under the AI Act for non-EU manufacturers or providers of AI-enabled medical devices.

sections.title: EU Importer - Pre-market Obligations
sections.answer_text: Under the AI Act, an EU importer of an AI-enabled medical device (classified as high-risk) must verify conformity before placing the system on the market, including checking for CE marking, EU declaration of conformity, and instructions for use; ensure storage and transport conditions do not jeopardize compliance; indicate their name, registered trade name or trademark, and contact address on the system, its packaging, or accompanying documentation; and keep a copy of the notified body's certificate, instructions for use, and EU declaration of conformity for 10 years after placement on the market.

sections.title: EU Importer - Post-market Obligations
sections.answer_text: Under the AI Act, an EU importer of an AI-enabled medical device (classified as a high-risk AI system) has specific post-market obligations, including: not placing the system on the market if it has sufficient reason to consider it non-conformant, falsified, or accompanied by falsified documentation until brought into conformity; informing the provider, authorized representative, and market surveillance authorities if the system presents a risk under Article 79(1); indicating their name, registered trade name or trademark, and contact address on the system, its packaging, or accompanying documentation; ensuring storage and transport conditions do not jeopardize compliance with requirements; keeping for 10 years after market placement a copy of the notified body's certificate (if applicable), instructions for use, and the EU declaration of conformity under Article 47; providing relevant competent authorities, upon reasoned request, with all necessary information and documentation to demonstrate conformity with Section 2 requirements in an understandable language, including ensuring technical documentation is available; and cooperating with competent authorities in actions related to the system to reduce and mitigate risks.

sections.title: EU Distributor - Pre-market Obligations
sections.answer_text: The provided evidence does not contain specific pre-market obligations for EU distributors of AI-enabled medical devices under the AI Act.

sections.title: EU Distributor - Post-market Obligations
sections.answer_text: The provided evidence does not contain specific information about the post-market obligations under the AI Act for an EU distributor of an AI-enabled medical device.

sections.title: Healthcare Organisation Deploying AI-enabled Medical Device - Pre-market Obligations
sections.answer_text: A healthcare organisation deploying an AI-enabled medical device that qualifies as a high-risk AI system under the AI Act must, as a provider, submit specific information for registration in the EU database before placing the system on the market or putting it into service. This includes: the provider's name, address, and contact details; details of any authorised representative; the AI system's trade name and unambiguous reference; a description of the intended purpose of the AI system and its components and functions; a basic description of the data inputs and operating logic; the system's market status; certificate details from the notified body (if applicable), including a scanned copy; Member States where the system is available; a copy of the EU declaration of conformity; electronic instructions for use; and an optional URL for additional information. The organisation must also ensure conformity with relevant Union harmonisation legislation (such as the Medical Devices Regulation) and may need to follow specific conformity assessment procedures, potentially involving notified bodies, depending on the device classification. Additionally, if the organisation considers the AI system not high-risk despite its inclusion in Annex III, it must document this assessment prior to market placement and be subject to registration under Article 49(2).

sections.title: Healthcare Organisation Deploying AI-enabled Medical Device - Post-market Obligations
